1. Outside view. The base rate for iPhone share in this basket typically sits around 39-41%, with Tesla at 9-10%, Samsung at 12-14%, Netflix at 17-18%, and Disney at 19-20%. In September, Apple holds its annual iPhone event, which represents the largest regular swing for this series. The iPhone's search volume typically spikes during the event week and remains highly elevated during the release week (the week after the event) at around 1.3x to 1.4x its normal baseline.

2. Inside view. The week being forecasted (Sept 13 - Sept 19, 2026) corresponds to the iPhone release week. The keynote event took place on Wednesday, Sept 9, and physical units launch on Friday, Sept 18. Crucially, 2026 introduces Apple's first foldable iPhone (rumored as "iPhone Ultra" or "iPhone Fold") alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup. This completely new form factor will drive substantially higher media and search interest than a standard iterative release year. Given the baseline sum of non-iPhone searches rests around 60 index points, an iPhone spike of 40% over baseline (driving its raw index from ~40 to ~56) would cause its share to climb to nearly 48-50%, proportionally compressing the other four brands by about 15% each. 

3. Pre-mortem. The most likely reason this turns out badly wrong is underestimating the magnitude of the hype for Apple's first foldable device. The search share could easily shatter typical release week multipliers, pushing iPhone up to 52-55% and crushing the remaining series into the low single or double digits. To correct for this, I've increased iPhone's expected share slightly above the historical 1.3x release-week bump and set a relatively wide standard deviation to capture this upside tail risk. 

4. Calibrate. With iPhone seeing such an aggressive demand surge, uncertainty will bleed into the other four brands as they fight for a mathematically smaller share of the sum. I will grant iPhone a standard deviation of 3.5 to easily encapsulate a range between a mild release bump (45%) and a massive foldable hype cycle (52%). The other SDs are similarly scaled to their absolute shares.
